Strait of Hormuz Status: October 2, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  215 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
2 October 2026 .
Brent $ 102.07 -0.23 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 Al Jazeera reports the US has moved 2,000 Marines to the Middle East amid ongoing tanker strikes in the Strait of Hormuz.

02 gCaptain reports another tanker was hit in the strait; the attacker has not been identified.

03 Brent stood at $102.07, down 0.23% over 24 hours, as of 05:56 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the focal point of an intensifying military and maritime crisis. Al Jazeera reports the United States has moved 2,000 Marines to the Middle East as part of a broader buildup around Iran, deploying the Roosevelt strike group alongside the force. Iranian state media, carried also by Türkiye Today, The Times of Israel, and Marine Insight, claim that Emirati oil tankers struck in the strait were on a non-compliance list; that is an Iranian government claim and has not been independently established. Al Jazeera and The Guardian report vessel attacks have resumed while Middle East crude exports have recovered to 80 percent of pre-war levels, though IMF PortWatch recorded only 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $102.07, down 0.23% over 24 hours, as of 05:56 UTC. Iran says it is reviewing the US response to Foreign Minister Araghchi's seven-day plan; President Trump rejected that plan publicly on September 26, and no new terms have been published. The site tracked 41 indexed events in the past 24 hours. As of 05:50 UTC, 115 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
